pr_title: Track exact ART size and many ART improvements
pr_body:
This PR adds logic to track the exact in-memory size of any existing ART index and many minor improvements. 

We update the current memory in the buffer manager after each operation on a chunk or after constructing an index via `CREATE INDEX ...`. Not all indexes propagate their in-memory size, i.e., transient indexes during ART creation or in the local state of a transaction do not propagate their in-memory size. To achieve this, the index contains a `track_memory` flag that identifies whether changes to the index's size should be propagated to the buffer manager. This closes #4967.

I also added a few micro-benchmarks to help spot significant index performance regressions in the future.

Other minor changes include the following (I know this PR got a bit too big - sooorry 😅):
- various comments and updated exception messages
- more assertions, especially in merge code
- removed some `static_cast` because I think we typically use regular casts in our code
- refactored `ART::VerifyExistence` by adding more precise exception messages and code paths
- recursively checking for side effects during `CREATE INDEX` plan creation
- refactored (de)serialization of leaf to match the cases for other node types
- node more magic numbers in the `cpp`-files of the different nodes
- handling of constraint checking when merging the thread-local ARTs into the global ART
pr_comments:
Thanks for the PR - LGTM. Perhaps it would be a good idea to implement a `Verify` method on the ART that verifies that the memory usage of all the nodes added together is equivalent to what is stored in the `ART::memory_usage` variable? This could be done by e.g. adding a recursive `GetUsedMemory` function to the ART nodes that is called in this verify method. 

In my experience it is easy for these types of variables that get incrementally updated to get out-of-sync because of bugs which might lead to hard-to-debug issues.

issue_context.title: Index sizes do not appear to be accounted for in pragma database_size
issue_context.body:
### What happens?

According to [this comment](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/issues/1546#issuecomment-1263525113) indexes should be managed by the buffer manager and thus contribute to the memory size listed when running `pragma database_size`. However, in some experiments with the CLI this doesn't appear to be the case.

I'm not sure if this is an actual bug or if I'm interpreting things incorrectly.

### To Reproduce

Below are some screenshots illustrating what I'm seeing. I was running duckdb built from commit 91a9fc49a5. So while not the absolute latest & greatest, it's pretty close.

The data being used is 100k rows of an integer and 10 varchars. It's contrived data, here's the first few rows
```csv
id,A0,A1,A2,A3,A4,A5,A6,A7,A8,A9,
0,"ccccccccccccccc00","ccccccccccccccc01","ccccccccccccccc02","ccccccccccccccc03","ccccccccccccccc04","ccccccccccccccc05","ccccccccccccccc06","ccccccccccccccc07","ccccccccccccccc08","ccccccccccccccc09",
1,"ccccccccccccccc10","ccccccccccccccc11","ccccccccccccccc12","ccccccccccccccc13","ccccccccccccccc14","ccccccccccccccc15","ccccccccccccccc16","ccccccccccccccc17","ccccccccccccccc18","ccccccccccccccc19",
2,"ccccccccccccccc20","ccccccccccccccc21","ccccccccccccccc22","ccccccccccccccc23","ccccccccccccccc24","ccccccccccccccc25","ccccccccccccccc26","ccccccccccccccc27","ccccccccccccccc28","ccccccccccccccc29",
```

In the first set of screenshots I've created a table with a primary key on the ID which will also create an index on that column. They show a discrepancy between what DuckDB is reporting versus what the OS is reporting.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8935186/195381451-4b6cd5a1-6310-4ad2-8eec-eed242a93874.png)
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8935186/195381526-c2f09aeb-d674-49c8-9174-070e666f25fa.png)

(The 0.4.0 and 0.5.1 instances of duckdb are running with the same table created from the same data set.)

The next set of screenshots show the same table loaded with the same data, except now the `id` column is not a primary key.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8935186/195381905-ffafb403-9582-473e-8ef1-63857ea78cd8.png)
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8935186/195381935-11b67b99-ccf3-44ea-b92b-e35ebe401fbf.png)

While I don't have a screenshot for it, if I manually create an index, `create index id_idx on t(id);` the OS-reported memory usage goes back up to about 41.0MB.


### OS:

MacOS

### DuckDB Version:

0.5.1

### DuckDB Client:

CLI

### Full Name:

Michael Albers

### Affiliation:

Mode

### Have you tried this on the latest `master` branch?

- [X] I agree

### Have you tried the steps to reproduce? Do they include all relevant data and configuration? Does the issue you report still appear there?

- [X] I agree
comments: @pdet or @taniabogatsch can one of you have a look at this issue?
This should be partially resolved by #5292 which adds approximate memory tracking to the ART index (pending exact memory tracking in a future PR).

If I remember correctly, these are all the places where I propagated changes to the buffermanager.
